blocks.content:
arXiv:1202.5426v2  [math.AP]  23 Jul 2012
Hard analysis meets critical knots
Stationary points of the M¨obius energy are smooth
S. Blatt∗
Φ. Reiter∗∗
A. Schikorra∗∗∗
June 30, 2018
We prove that if a curve γ ∈H3/2(R/Z, Rn) parametrized by arc length is a sta-
tionary point of the M¨obius energy introduced by Jun O’Hara in [O’H91], then γ
is smooth. Our methods only rely on purely analytical arguments, entirely with-
out using M¨obius invariance. Furthermore, they are not fundamentally restricted
to one-dimensional domains, but are generalizable to arbitrary dimensions.
Contents
1. Introduction

blocks.title: Stationary points are smooth
blocks.content: Any stationary point γ ∈H 2 (R/Z, Rn) of E(2), i.e., any curve γ ∈H 2 (R/Z, Rn) for which δE(2)(γ; h) = 0 for all h ∈C∞(R/Z, Rn), belongs to C∞when parametrized by arc-length. In [BR12], improving a previous result [Rt12], the smoothness of stationary points of ﬁnite energy was already shown for the case of E(α) := E(α,1), α ∈(2, 3), instead of the M¨obius energy. It is worth noting, that those energies lead to a subcritical Euler-Langrage equation, and that in some sense the regularity theory can be based on Sobolev embeddings for fractional Sobolev and Besov spaces.
